idiom_name: Slick TableQuery for the link table with an explicit join
implementation_notes: Slick is a functional-relational mapper: it never hides the schema, so the association is a TableQuery of its own with the two foreign-key columns and a primaryKey over the pair, and the collection is produced by composing join queries (actorFilm.filter(_.actorId === aid).join(films).on(_.filmId === _.id)). Insertion and deletion of link rows are ordinary table operations, which is the hand-written half of the pattern with typed queries instead of strings. Because nothing tracks the association, uniqueness, orphan cleanup and batched loading (groupBy for many owners, or a join over a set of ids) are the developer's responsibility.
pitfalls: Slick runs on JDBC: blocking calls must be pushed onto a dedicated execution context, or a large collection load starves the pool other code shares.
A missing primaryKey/unique index lets += insert the same pair repeatedly; Slick will not object.
Joins are composed explicitly, so the N+1 pattern reappears as one query per actor when the code is written in a loop rather than a grouped or joined query.
Orphan link rows are not cleaned up by Slick: either declare the foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE in the DDL or delete links explicitly in the same transaction.
